heading: Occurrence count — `exactly N`
text:
### Occurrence count — `exactly N` [LTSL.8.7]

A head may carry the modifier `exactly <N>`, asserting the observation occurred
**exactly N times** over the run.

`exactly` composes with matching ([LTSL.8.4]) and with `where` unchanged: the
count is of observations that match, not of all observations under the head.

**`exactly` refines polarity, it does not replace it.** A bare head is `POS`
(at least once) and `never` is zero times ([LTSL.8.3]); `exactly N` states the
exact tally on that same axis. `never <head> exactly <N>` has no single reading
and the compiler must reject it.

The count is an **equality**. The surface admits no `at least` or `at most`
form: `at least 1` is a bare head, and no other comparison has been asked for.

`N` is at least 1. `exactly 0` is not admitted — `never` is that assertion, and
admitting a second spelling for it would put two forms on one meaning. This
also keeps the wire encoding free of a presence flag: the atom carries a plain
count whose zero reads as "no occurrence constraint", which is the
`proto3 zero = absent` convention the rest of the corpus uses.

```{admonition} exactly N is a whole-run tally, not a per-trigger claim
:class: warning
It cannot distinguish two rules firing on ONE trigger from one rule firing on
TWO — both are two occurrences. So `published X exactly 1` constrains a
single-trigger scenario and nothing wider; in a scenario that pumps more than
once it will fail on correct programs.

To assert that two rules never both fire, use `exclusive` ([LTSL.8.8]), which
is scoped rather than tallied.
```

**The `wm` head does not admit `exactly`, and the compiler must reject it.**
`wm has` / `wm count` / `wm empty` inspect working memory at the END of the run
([LTSL.8.6]); they observe a state, not a stream of occurrences, so there is
nothing for an occurrence tally to count. `wm count <Schema> == N` keeps its own
spelling and is not an instance of this modifier: there `count` is the head and
the number is a final-state **cardinality**, while `exactly` is a modifier and
the number is an occurrence **tally**.

The exclusion is deliberate and costs a wart — the modifier reads as "every
head except one". The alternative is worse: one head carrying two different
meanings for a number, where `wm count == 2` and `wm has … exactly 2` would
look like the same assertion and be different ones, with nothing in the surface
to tell them apart. A reader can look up an exclusion; a reader cannot see a
conflated meaning.
